chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is a right upon the Muslim that when he intends to travel, he should inform his brothers, and it is a right upon his brothers that when he returns, they should visit him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the mutual rights of Muslims regarding travel and return?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of al-Kulayni, emphasizes the social contract of *mu'akhat* (brotherhood) by mandating proactive communication from the traveler and attentive visitation from the community upon return. In Shia jurisprudence, this is viewed not merely as etiquette but as a fulfilled right (*haqq*) that strengthens communal bonds and ensures the well-being of the individual within the collective. It reflects the broader Islamic principle that social cohesion requires active maintenance through both departure and return rituals.
